## TuiControllerBase renderer clipping

- Currently the TUI render target supports clipper.
- Clipping must be implemented in VlppOS's TUI instead of in render target.
  - In this way we could keep DRY.
  - A clipper will be passed to any drawing functions. It could be a TuiClipper struct with x1,y1,x2,y2 in `vint`.
    - In drawing functions, we can first create a clipper equals to the buffer range, and see if null pointer comes in, if not do intersection.
    - In drawing functions such "normalized" clipper will be first calculated and then draw.
  - Render target could just simply calling them in this way.

### DETAILS

- The existing raster clipping belongs to `TuiGraphicsRenderTarget` in `Source/PlatformProviders/TUI/TuiGraphics.cpp`. Keep the render target's composition clip stack (`PushClipper`, `PopClipper`, and effective-clip queries); move the drawing primitives' clipping into VlppOS. The stack still defines the clip passed to each drawing call.
- Add `vl::console::TuiClipper` alongside the TUI drawing types in `../VlppOS/Source/TUI/TUI.h`, with `vint` coordinates and half-open bounds `[x1, x2) x [y1, y2)`. Append an optional `const TuiClipper*` parameter, defaulting to `nullptr`, to both the active-buffer and explicit-buffer overloads of every drawing operation: `TUI::PrintChar`, `TUI::Clear`, `TUI::DrawLineV`, `TUI::DrawLineH`, and `TUI::DrawRect`. Rounded corners remain an option on `TUI::DrawRect`.
- Normalize the clip against the current buffer dimensions inside VlppOS. Null means the whole buffer; empty, inverted, or disjoint intersections paint nothing. Preserve existing argument validation even when nothing is visible. Existing inclusive drawing endpoints remain unchanged; GacUI converts its exclusive rectangle edges once when forming those endpoints.
- Clip the original geometry, rather than replacing its endpoints with the clip bounds. In particular, a clip inside a rectangle must not create new edges or corners. Preserve line merging, rounded-corner rules, one-cell-wide/high borders, and the existing GacUI 1-by-1 border no-op.
- Preserve width-two cell invariants. A new wide glyph requires both cells inside the normalized clip before any mutation. Overwriting an existing lead or continuation cell may clear its partner immediately outside the clip, as required by the existing wide-cell repair contract; this is the only permitted repair spill outside the clip. Keep the partner's background and leave unrelated cells untouched.
- VlppOS TUI colors do not contain GacUI alpha. Retain GacUI's destination-dependent RGB blending, transparent no-ops, text styles/backgrounds, and caret behavior. Any destination reads in the render target must still be in bounds before calling the clipped primitive. Reacquire the buffer and dimensions for each operation, including after nested resize callbacks. Do not introduce GacUI types into VlppOS.
- Replace the full-buffer scratch copy used for opaque borders with direct clipped VlppOS drawing. Keep any alpha-specific work proportional to affected cells; do not retain a second implementation of geometry clipping in GacUI.
- Make upstream changes in the sibling VlppOS source repository, follow its guidance, and regenerate its release and GacUI imports through the supported dependency workflow. GacUI compiles `Import/VlppOS.*`; editing only the sibling source does not update its dependency. Do not hand-edit generated release/import files. Update the owning TUI API/KB documentation when implementing the new contract.

## TUI Color Theme

- Add multiple predefined color options, allow changing them on the fly in `TuiControlTest`.
  - This is done by asking every window to recreate control templates recursively.
- General implementation:
  - Currently we have a `CreateDefaultColorPackage` for sky blue. We need to create:
    - `CreatePinkColorPackage`
    - `CreateOrangeColorPackage`
    - `CreateGrassPackage`
    - `CreateEmeraldPackage`
    - `CreateSkyblueColorPackage`
    - `CreatePurplePackage`
  - All these colors will not be pure and extreme colors, you need to pick a good one, you may want to get the idea from the internet.
  - And you will find them sharing a lot of code, so a internal function `CreateColorPackageInternal` could be created and every function just calls it.
  - `CreateDefaultColorPackage` will then call `CreateSkyblueColorPackage` internally.
  - Now we need a function to recreate control themes. Calling `SetColorPackage` won't update any existing color, the easiest way is to recreate all control themes.
    - `GuiApplication::RefreshThemes` function will be added for this, in this way it find all living `GuiWindow` instances and call its `RefreshThemes` function.
    - `GuiControl::RefreshThemes` will recreate theme inside recursively to all sub controls. A menu button doesn't need to care about its dropdown as it will be taken care of by `GuiApplication::RefreshThemes`, and a dropdown is not technically a child control of menu button anyway. So the implementation should be straight forward.
    - `GuiControl::RefreshThemes` should only work when its `ControlTemplate` is not assigned, as this property is designed to override the theme. Ideally it should just call `RebuildControlTemplate` for itself and recursively call other `RefreshThemes`.
- Verification
  - In `TuiControlTest`'s `Window Manager` page, split the page in half horizontally and in the right side we could put a group box with radio buttons listed in a vertical stack, set to `SkyBlue (default)`. When any button is clicked, it calls `SetColorPackage` and `GetApplication()->RefreshThemes` in `InvokeInMainThread`.

### DETAILS

- Implement the six factories with the exact names above in the manually maintained `Test/GacUISrc/Generated_TuiSkin/TuiSkinConfig.h/.cpp`. Share neutral colors and complete field initialization in `tuiskin::CreateColorPackageInternal`; vary a coordinated muted accent and darker highlight for focused borders, selected items, highlighted buttons, and highlighted menu/list items. Keep normal surfaces, normal/disabled text, normal borders, and shortcut-label colors common across presets. Preserve the existing palette values in `tuiskin::CreateSkyblueColorPackage`, and make `tuiskin::CreateDefaultColorPackage` return that package.
- Add public parameterless `void RefreshThemes()` methods to `GuiControl` and `GuiApplication` in `Source/Application/Controls/GuiBasicControls.h/.cpp` and `GuiApplication.h/.cpp`. They perform synchronous work on the UI thread and remain generic GUI APIs, without a TUI dependency. Register both methods in `Source/Reflection/TypeDescriptors/GuiReflectionControls.cpp` so Workflow can call them. `GuiWindow` inherits the control method.
- For `GuiControl::RefreshThemes`, a nonempty `ControlTemplate` skips only that control's own rebuild, not traversal of its descendants. For an unassigned template, reuse `RebuildControlTemplate` and its install/uninstall hooks without assigning the resolved factory to `ControlTemplate`. Traverse the live child-control tree after rebuilding the parent, because rebuilding destroys and recreates template-owned controls. Preserve application-owned controls and their container compositions.
- `GuiApplication::RefreshThemes` uses its existing `windows` registry, including hidden windows and popups, rather than only the main window or `openingPopups`. Do not recursively refresh a menu button's separate dropdown from that button. Snapshot windows with their existing `GuiDisposedFlag` objects and skip disposed entries before dereferencing them: rebuilding a date-picker template replaces its year/month combos and their registered popup windows. Apply the same lifetime discipline to child snapshots taken after parent reconstruction. Newly constructed themed controls already use the installed palette; do not chase an expanding registry.
- An assigned template includes factories installed by another control, not only assignments authored in application XML. `GuiMenuButton::CreateSubMenu` in `Source/Controls/ToolstripPackage/GuiMenuControls.cpp` currently assigns the owner's `SubMenuTemplate` to the popup's `ControlTemplate`. These popup templates remain exempt under the requested rule, but their themed descendants still refresh. The retained TUI menu/content-popup frames use only the shared neutral roles (`MenuBackground`, `ControlBackground`, and `ControlBorder`), so this does not leave an old accent. Keep caller-supplied overrides intact, including borderless grid editor templates. `GuiDateComboBox` already reapplies its date-picker template in its install hook; cover that path as well.
- Palette values captured by application-owned `Color-eval` elements also survive control-template rebuilding. Examples are `SolidLabel` and `TuiBorder` elements in the showcase's date-picker, localized, embedded-control, and responsive pages. Their neutral roles remain common across these presets. Do not claim that `SetColorPackage` alone makes arbitrary element colors or custom templates reactive.
- Repeated template replacement exercises existing lifecycle problems that must be fixed as part of implementation:
  - `GuiMenuButton::BeforeControlTemplateUninstalled_` detaches `hostClickedHandler` from `Clicked`, but the install hook attaches it to `BeforeClicked`. Detach from the matching event so refreshing menus/combos does not accumulate callbacks.
  - Document template-install hooks in `Source/Controls/TextEditorPackage/GuiDocumentViewer.cpp` call `SetDocument(GetDocument())`. This path copies the document, clears undo/redo and modified state in `GuiDocumentCommonInterface.cpp`, and resets caret state in `GuiDocumentElement`. Refresh baseline/caret colors without resetting the existing document, selection, undo/redo, or modified state.
  - Scroll-view bars are template-owned controls, recreated during a rebuild in `Source/Controls/GuiContainerControls.cpp`. Preserve the logical view position through template replacement and layout, clamping only when the valid range changes. Refreshing colors must not unexpectedly scroll every list/editor back to the origin.
  - `ListViewColumnItemArranger` in `Source/Controls/ListControlPackage/GuiListViewControls.cpp` retains column-header controls with assigned `ColumnHeaderTemplate` factories. Refresh these owner-supplied templates through the list-view/arranger install lifecycle, preserving column identity, width, sorting, and dropdowns. The generic explicit-template skip rule alone would leave their TUI accent colors stale.
  - Detaching the persistent content composition during a rebuild disconnects it from `GuiGraphicsHost` and clears actual keyboard focus. Capture surviving user-control focus and affected state before ancestor reconstruction, and restore focus to the still-live control afterward. Setting a template's `Focused` flag alone does not restore keyboard input; do not retain destroyed template-owned controls.
- Interpret the page split as left and right halves: use two equal percentage columns, keep the existing Window Manager controls on the left, and put a group box containing six vertically stacked radio buttons on the right. Use one `GuiSelectableButton::MutexGroupController`, select `SkyBlue (default)` initially, and retain that selection after refresh. Apply the cell-layout rules in `GacUILayout.md`, including zero unnecessary padding and useful content at 80x25.
- The palette factories and `SetColorPackage` are currently native C++ helpers, not Workflow functions. Keep the XML/C++ boundary explicit: expose a palette-selection event/property on the generated main window from `Resource.xml`, and wire it once in `Test/GacUISrc/CppTest_Tui/Main.cpp` to the native factories. Queue `SetColorPackage` followed by `GetApplication()->RefreshThemes()` together through `InvokeInMainThread`, capturing the selected preset by value. Refresh after the input callback has returned, not while its template is being used. Handle only the newly selected radio button, and avoid queueing another refresh while restoring existing selection. This must work in the showcase's no-reflection build.
- When implementing, update `GacUILayout.md` and `.github/KnowledgeBase/KB_GacUI_Design_TuiPlatformProvider.md` to describe all factories, live refresh, and the override/captured-color scope; their current descriptions list only two helpers and startup-time installation. # TEST [CONFIRMED]

The first regression in `../VlppOS/Test/Source/TestTui.cpp` checks all ten drawing signatures for an optional clipper. It compiles against the existing API using a dependent requires-expression and fails at runtime until clipped overloads exist. Behavioral tests will compare distinguishable seeded buffers across null/full/interior/partial/exterior/empty/inverted clips, all primitives and both overload families, original corners, mixed line merging, invalid arguments, zero-sized buffers and wide-glyph repairs. Every active-buffer result must pass `TUI::RenderBuffer`.

GacUI regressions will cover nested/empty clips, resize with a live clip, opaque and alpha drawing, wide carets, and one clear/present per hosted frame. Theme regressions will cover explicit overrides, disposed popup/child snapshots, generic GUI theme replacement, focus, document/selection/history/modified state, scroll offsets, retained column headers and menu callback counts. Required metadata/resource generation, completed wrapper logs and Debug leak reports are part of acceptance. Actual Windows Terminal operations from the TUI SOP will be recorded separately from buffer tests.

The baseline Debug x64 wrapper build succeeded with zero warnings/errors. The UnitTest wrapper exited 1 at `All drawing overloads accept an optional clipper`, with `Assertion failure: supportsClipping.operator()<TUI>()`; the new test confirms the missing public clipping contract. Existing tests before that point passed. This is API reproduction, not terminal verification.

# PROPOSALS

- No.1 Centralize clipped drawing in VlppOS and preserve generic control state during live theme refresh. [CONFIRMED]

## No.1 Centralize clipped drawing in VlppOS and preserve generic control state during live theme refresh

Normalize the optional half-open clip in VlppOS after argument validation. Restrict writes before wide-pair mutation, retain original rectangle endpoints and reuse existing glyph merging and partner repair. GacUI keeps its composition clip stack and destination-dependent colors, passing the effective clip to the primitives. Opaque borders draw directly; alpha work must use the same rasterization boundary rather than cloning clipping rules.

Implement the six native palette factories and deferred showcase selection. Add generic reflected refresh methods that rebuild only unassigned templates, snapshot the live post-rebuild child tree and registered windows with disposed flags, and preserve focus. Fix document template hooks, scrollbar state, retained list headers and the mismatched menu event detachment at their owners. Generate resources and metadata through repository wrappers and update the owning documentation.

### CODE CHANGE

- `../VlppOS/Source/TUI/TUI.h/.cpp`: add the optional half-open `TuiClipper` to all ten drawing overloads. Normalize against current buffer dimensions after argument validation, reject invisible writes before wide-pair mutation, and clip original line/rectangle geometry without inventing edges. Preserve merging, rounded corners and existing partner-background repair. An optional synchronous foreground-color transform in line/rectangle options lets GacUI blend alpha only at painted cells, without duplicating rasterization or copying the buffer. It must not mutate or pump TUI state.
- Regenerate upstream Release with CodePack and update GacUI's Import pair through the supported dependency copy. SHA-256 hashes of both Import files match upstream Release. The upstream owning TUI KB documents clipping and the color transform.
- `Source/PlatformProviders/TUI/TuiGraphics.cpp/.h`: retain the composition clip stack, forward its clip to VlppOS, remove the border scratch buffer and duplicated perimeter clipping, and preserve safe destination reads, alpha/text/background/style and wide-caret behavior across resize.
- `Source/Application/Controls/GuiBasicControls.cpp/.h`, `GuiApplication.cpp/.h`, and `Source/Reflection/TypeDescriptors/GuiReflectionControls.cpp`: add reflected, synchronous UI-thread `RefreshThemes` APIs. Rebuild only unassigned templates; snapshot live children after rebuilding and registered windows before iteration with disposed flags. Preserve explicit overrides and surviving application-owned control focus.
- `Source/Controls/GuiContainerControls.cpp/.h`: transfer scrollbar ranges, page sizes and positions before attaching replacement-bar handlers; normal layout clamps the new valid range. `Source/Controls/ListControlPackage/GuiListControls.cpp` preserves positions around row reloads and reloads only visible styles during render-target changes, retaining the unchanged provider and arranger.
- `Source/Controls/TextEditorPackage/GuiDocumentViewer.cpp`: preserve complete baseline formatting on first template installation. Subsequent installs update font/baseline/caret colors without replacing the model or clearing edits, selection, undo/redo or modified state. `GuiListViewControls.cpp` reapplies retained header factories while preserving identity, widths, sorting and filter dropdowns. `GuiMenuControls.cpp` detaches the handler from the matching `BeforeClicked` event.
- `Test/GacUISrc/Generated_TuiSkin/TuiSkinConfig.h/.cpp`: expose all six exact factory names, share every neutral role, vary coordinated accent/highlight colors, and keep Default forwarding to the unchanged SkyBlue values. The authored `Resource.xml` adds equal columns, one six-radio mutex group and a generated palette event. `CppTest_Tui/Main.cpp` captures the preset by value and queues native palette installation plus refresh after input dispatch. Both architectures' generated sources/resources come from `GacUI_Compiler`.
- Extend upstream primitive tests, `TestTuiProvider.cpp` and `TestApplication_Theme.cpp`. Coverage includes clipping/repair/resize/alpha, palettes, disposed popup registry mutation, explicit parent/leaf overrides, retained headers and content/date popups, open modal refresh, real keyboard focus, document identity/history/selection/modified state, TAB/Shift+TAB, tree/list selection and nonzero view offsets after deferred layout. An initial GUI transparency assertion protects the first-install baseline path.
- Update `GacUILayout.md`, the TUI provider and list-control architecture KBs, and `.github/Jobs/DebugTuiControlTestSop.md` with the owning contracts and concrete replay observations. Assigned templates and application-owned captured element colors remain outside automatic recoloring as specified.

The staged list regression first established an accepted (5,10) position, then proved it became (0,0) after refresh. CDB's data breakpoint traced the first write through ancestor-container detachment, `OnRenderTargetChanged`, `SetStyleAndArranger`, `DetachCallback`, `SetItemSource(nullptr)` and `Layout_ResetLayout`. With no host, `CalculateView` ran synchronously during that artificial empty-data interval and disabled both bars. Retaining the provider/arranger during visible-row reload avoids it; restoring the position around both list lifecycle hooks survives subsequent queued layout. Explicit item-template/arranger changes retain their reset semantics.

The first complete GacUI run passed 90/90 files and 1,755/1,755 cases without leaks, but snapshot review found opaque backgrounds in initially constructed plain-text controls. The replacement hook had omitted the original first-install baseline formatting. Keeping initialization separate from refresh restores the transparent default while preserving state during later refreshes. The corrected focused replay passes all 22 cases, including the new transparency assertion. The final complete wrapper run passes 90/90 files and 1,755/1,755 cases with no leak dump.

Generation and architecture validation are complete: pre-resource Debug Win32/x64 metadata generation and x64 Metadata_Test passed; the full resource compiler generated and merged both architectures without UI error files; the required post-generation metadata sequence passed; final Debug x64 and Win32 builds after the lifecycle corrections both report zero warnings/errors. Workflow event handlers require braces around their if bodies; that authored-XML syntax correction was regenerated normally.

The SOP records controlled pseudoterminal replay on both architectures. All six palettes and return to SkyBlue pass mouse and keyboard at 120x40 and 80x25 with exactly one selected radio and matching emitted RGB. Existing child windows, edited/sorted/filtered grids, recycled list rows, scrolled edited documents, mouse/keyboard menu actions, shortcuts and fake dialogs survive palette changes. Post-correction x64/Win32 smoke runs under architecture-matched CDB exit 0 with no leak dump and restore console modes, viewport, attributes and cursor. ### CONFIRMED

The final Debug x64 wrapper log reports 90/90 files and 1,755/1,755 cases passed with no assertion failure or Debug leak dump. VlppOS's completed wrapper log reports 16/16 files and 306/306 cases passed without leaks. Both final GacUI architecture builds have zero warnings/errors, both metadata sequences and x64 metadata validation passed, and the resource compiler completed both architectures without error files.

All existing GUI frame content matches the baseline. Only ScrollResetOnNavigation's frame IDs and intermediate rendering traces differ: JSON comparison excluding frameId proves the saved frame structures, properties, geometry and text are identical. The seven timing-only snapshot files were restored after saving their diff in the verification artifacts. New theme regression snapshots are retained.

The proposal centralizes clipping at the primitive boundary while retaining GacUI alpha behavior, and the owner lifecycle fixes preserve meaningful control state through refresh and subsequent layout/input. Console replay additionally verifies palette selection and emitted RGB, existing/new controls, menus, editors, lists/grids, nested dropdowns, dialogs, resizing, normal shutdown and console restoration. The detailed operations and architecture-specific smoke/leak checks are recorded in the TUI SOP.

Windows Terminal's displayed appearance and physical keyboard/mouse delivery remain unverified because the computer-use tool rejected its launch under product policy.
